issues.body: `parse_float` still maps both `INF` and `+INF` to positive infinity. The XSD float/double special lexical representations are `INF`, `-INF`, and `NaN`; `+INF` is not valid. This contradicts the generated module's claim that floating-point lexical well-formedness is enforced. The datatype harness still covers no xsd:float or xsd:double behavior, so the real generated-loader path remains untested for this case.
issues.fix_hint: Remove `+INF` from the accepted special forms and extend the generated-loader behavioral harness with xsd:float and xsd:double properties. Test acceptance of `INF`, `-INF`, `NaN`, and ordinary decimal/exponent forms, and rejection of `+INF`, Rust-only spellings such as `inf`/`infinity`, case variants, whitespace, and malformed numeric forms.
issues.title: Floating-point validator still accepts the non-XSD `+INF` lexical form

verdict.summary: Round 4 leaves the round-3 major correctness finding unresolved. The generated loader still accepts `+INF` for both xsd:float and xsd:double even though XSD permits only `INF`, `-INF`, and `NaN` as special lexical forms. The behavioral datatype harness still contains no float/double cases, so it does not exercise the advertised floating-point lexical validation. Progress is stagnant because the same major issue remains at the same severity.
